newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares rise despite profit fears.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares rise despite profit fears.

text.p: Fears that quoted Nigerian oil products marketers are poised to post poor results next week failed to weaken their stocks by close of trading this week.
Continued offloading of blue chips in other sectors, however, persisted. The all-share index closed marginally lower at 6,621.17 on Friday from 6,621.18 on Thursday.
Traders expressed concern that oil companies were stalling in releasing their results, expected over the last weeks, because of anticipated lower profits.
All but one of the marketers rose, led by Unipetrol which touched a record 44.00 naira from 43.50 naira on Thursday.
Total notched 20 kobo to 49.05 naira while African Petroleum, Mobil and National Oil each rose 20 kobo at 35.20 naira, 41.50 naira and 36.70 naira, respectively.
"The results they are about to post could be a ploy to persuade government to heed their call for a better profit margin," said James Odife of brokerage Centre-Point Investments.
Oil firms have been seeking a review of their memorandum of understanding with state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp to boost their profit margins.
Conglomerates were the biggest losers in the market on Friday. John Holt fell nine kobo to 10.30 naira, UAC was down five kobo at 9.60 naira and CFAO lost one kobo at 3.99 naira.
Nigerian Breweries slid to 11.15 naira, five kobo lower, the same as Cadbury which closed at 26.35 naira.
Nestle Foods was up 50 kobo at 37.30 naira on a continued positive perception following its impressive half-year result.
Traders said the market trend would remain bearish as investors normally sell stocks at this time of year to meet seasonal Christmas and end of year expenses.
